name: Do you need a permit to convert a bathtub into a shower in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do you need a permit to convert a bathtub into a shower in Los Angeles or nearby cities?
mainEntity.text: Do you need a permit to convert a bathtub into a shower in Los Angeles or nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Los Angeles area, a tub-to-shower conversion often needs a permit because it usually changes plumbing, drainage, or the bathroom’s waterproofing system. The requirement can depend on the scope of work and the city, but most full conversions are more than cosmetic updates. Projects that move the drain, replace the valve, alter framing, or change the shower pan typically need approval. Homeowners should verify requirements before demolition starts, because unpermitted plumbing work can create inspection problems later when selling or refinancing. A good contractor should explain what will be permitted, what inspections are expected, and whether the work will be signed off by the local building department. This is especially important in cities with older housing stock, where hidden code issues are common. Always ask whether permit fees, plan review, and inspection coordination are included in the quote so the project schedule and budget stay realistic.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a permit is commonly required when the conversion changes plumbing, drainage, or structural elements. If the project only replaces finishes without moving fixtures, permit requirements may be different, but a tub-to-shower conversion usually involves plumbing and waterproofing work that triggers review.
